content:
elena: Heads-up: planning to GA the Hosted 'fastlane' streaming endpoint next Tue. This thread is the cross-functional prep checklist for marketing, docs, legal, and oncall. Short summary: GA means enabling the opt-in endpoint `POST /v2/fast-lane/stream` for all hosted customers (no default opt-in), publishing docs, and a customer-facing banner with migration notes.

matt: Outline the rollout steps here and I'll hook up synthetic checks to the new endpoint.

elena: Rollout steps: 
1) Finalize docs + migration guide (nora)
2) Legal review of TOS & rate limit language (zara)
3) Support runbook & canned responses (sara)
4) Monitoring/alerts live and synthetic checks (matt)
5) Dashboard banner and API changelog entry (nora)
6) GA announcement email + blog (marketing)

nora: Docs PR is in flight: https://git.internal/docs/hosted/fastlane-ga. I added an FAQ section: expected latency targets, how to opt-in, header `X-Redwood-Low-Latency`, and per-tool limits. ETA for merge: EOD Mon.

zara: Legal: will review the rate-limit wording and any implications of 'low-latency' guarantees. Expect questions about SLA phrasing. Can you tag specific commit/wording for us to review?

elena: Tagging the PR now. We will not add any SLA in GA copy; it's a QoS opt-in with best-effort. If customers want contractual SLAs we route to Dedicated/reserved capacity.

sara: Support: I'll draft canned responses for common asks: "how to opt-in", "why am I getting 429s for tool calls", and "how fast is fast-lane vs standard". Also need escalation matrix for oncall.

matt: Monitoring: synthetic checks posted to dashboard: stream-connect success, stream-first-byte latency, kv-cache-warm hit rate. I'll create a pager rule: page when stream-first-byte P95 > 200ms for 3m or if synthetic failure rate > 1% for 5m.

ops-bot: Release job started by elena at 1900603600: job-id=fastlane-ga-3001, health-check=running.

liam: Marketing: short blog draft ready. We need a customer quote; anyone internal using it in prod?

elena: A couple of early partners are on Canary—I'll ask for opt-in quotes. Also we should include a short tech note on how batching windows are reduced and why KV warmup matters.

nora: Dashboard banner text proposal: "New: Fast-lane streaming (opt-in). Lower latency for interactive apps. See docs for migration and rate limits." Approve?

sara: Looks good; add a link to support contact for rate-limit exceptions.

zara: Legal: approved the language as long as we don't imply guaranteed latency. Approved banner with minor edits.

matt: Ops note: ensure incident playbook has steps to rollback GA flag if we see fallback rates spike. I'll add runbook step: `toggle fastlane-ga flag -> rollback -> invalidate warm caches`

elena: Final QA: test plan includes: 1) opt-in header acceptance and rejection path, 2) ensure headers `X-Tool-Rate-Limit` and `X-Tool-Rate-Remaining` present, 3) simulate tool-calling storm and validate throttling to 15 calls/min per-tool per-key, 4) validate fallbacks.invoked metric increments when overloaded.

liam: Timeline: docs merged by Mon EOD, legal sign-off Mon night, support canned responses Mon night, GA announcement Tue 10:00 PT. Marketing will coordinate email send window.

elena: Thanks. If anything blocks sign-off ping me directly. We'll keep this thread updated with final links and the live GA post. :tada:
